subject: Energy
title: Boiling Water Reactors
description: A quick, practical guide to Boiling Water Reactors.

hook.text: In a BWR, water boils directly inside the reactor core—steam goes straight to the turbine, no secondary loop needed.

buildup.text: Simpler design means lower cost—but the steam is slightly radioactive, so the turbine area needs shielding.

discovery.text: About 60 BWRs operate worldwide—the second most common type, popular in the US and Japan.

twist.text: Fukushima's reactors were BWRs—their design performed as intended during the earthquake but not the tsunami.

climax.text: Modern BWR designs add passive safety—gravity-fed water systems that work without power or human intervention.

punchline.text: Simpler plumbing, same physics—water boils right in the core.

quiz.question: How does a BWR differ from a PWR?
options: Water boils directly in the reactor core
